works.title: (Water) Townies
works.blurb: A city sim of the real Watertown, MA, built to scale from assessor records, with scenarios lifted from local news comment sections and a real traffic model under the hood. Ask any problem "Why?" and it shows you the chain of causes. To see its innards, open Help → Behind the Scenes.

works.title: Ambit: Quartet
works.blurb: Four ambient instruments in one iPhone app, each listening to a different invisible field around you. Aether Wave plays the Bluetooth radio in the room, Bellweathered drones the weather, Leitmotif turns your phone's own data traffic into a melody, and Orbitakt drums the satellites passing overhead. A pad on the home screen leans the mix toward one voice.

works.title: Big Apple Sam
works.blurb: A night skyline from an old screensaver you might half remember, rebuilt. Zoom into any lit window and someone is living their life in there. It also comes as a real Mac screen saver that runs the city across every display.

works.title: HomeBlocks
works.blurb: Every resident of Big Apple Sam has a homepage the way people made them in 1998: tiled backgrounds, guestbooks, webrings, a MIDI tune and an Under Construction sign that never comes down. Each page is written from that person's life in the city, so it changes when their life does. Click through to see their window in the skyline, then back to their page.

works.title: Orders of Magnitude
works.blurb: One seed played as a demoscene production at five size limits, each a step in time: 4K in 1995 up to 40M in 2026. Every bigger limit buys more sound and more song structure, from tracker loops to trance builds, EDM drops and a cinematic score.

works.title: MEGAzine BBS
works.blurb: The collective's own dial-up BBS, and where outside submissions come in. One caller at a time unless the sysop adds phone lines; message boards, files with upload/download ratios, rumors of a secret login, and door games, including Matt's ChairQuest, where you try to survive a year as department chair.

works.title: Decay Envelope
works.blurb: A puzzle adventure set inside a eurorack synthesizer. A depressed old man, a world of terminally online people, and a lot of patch cables.

works.title: Brick Ninja
works.blurb: A side-scrolling ninja made of bricks, vibe coded with a five-year-old. Ninja stars, double jumps, and hidden doors into first-person bonus rooms where the overpowered weapons live.

works.title: Toilet Goalie
works.blurb: A five-year-old vibe coded this: the goalie is a toilet, you flick the ball to shoot, and it fights back.

works.title: Bell Weather
works.blurb: A drone-and-bell machine played by today's weather and the hour where you are. It started life as a script for a small music computer.

works.title: DialUpSoundz
works.blurb: Paste a chat assistant's playlist and it lands in Apple Music. It picks original studio versions over live and karaoke ones. A one-time unlock adds ratings, tags, liner notes and listening history, all kept on your phone, and its Operator lets your chat assistant recommend from your actual taste.

works.title: Rehearsal Loop
works.platform: iPhone, iPad · Apple Music or your own songs
works.blurb: Tap at the start and end of the part you're learning, and it plays that part over and over until you've got it. Songs you own slow down without changing pitch. A one-time Pro unlock shows the loop's notes and chords, and lets you play along with your part muted.

works.title: Animal Sanctuary
works.blurb: Find glowing foxes and small dragons in a magical world, bring them home, and grow them a sanctuary.

works.title: Titanosaur
works.platform: Album by Thunderblitz · on every streaming service
works.blurb: The Thunderblitz album. No code, no prompts, just music.

works.title: Topple House
works.blurb: Dominoes, where the levels are rooms of a house: bedroom, kitchen, hallway, stairs. Place them anywhere, preview the fall, then knock it down.

works.title: Solstice
works.blurb: Photograph a headstone at Mount Auburn Cemetery and it works out who is buried there, then lays out what the records actually say. Sourced facts stay apart from guesses.

works.title: The Palace
works.blurb: A haunted-mansion survival game whose puzzles quietly measure spatial memory while you try to save the man who let the ghouls in.

works.title: Mind Arcade
works.blurb: A neuropsych test battery disguised as arcade games. It picks the next game based on how sure it is about you so far.

works.title: Mise en Place
works.blurb: A frantic kitchen game that estimates your attentional capacity from how you juggle the orders.

works.title: Crush Commando
works.blurb: A shooter about destroying your own sadness, and what you turn into once it's gone.

works.title: MINERVA Space Echo
works.blurb: A tape echo that remembers every bar you play. Each bar is its own memory trace, and what comes back is a blend of all of them, weighted by how much each sounds like what you're playing now.

works.title: PCASynth and PCAWave
works.blurb: Two synths that turn one note, played by different instruments, into a space you can play. You get the originals, blends of them, and places no instrument has been. One rebuilds every point from its harmonics; its twin mixes the recordings themselves.

works.title: Metamers
works.blurb: A button that writes a scientific paper that was never written, with figures, observers and statistics that agree with one another. It is built from twenty-two years of one vision lab's papers, in about the weight of a single one of them.

works.title: ChairQuest
works.blurb: A quest game in which you try to survive a year as a university department chair. It's silly, and mostly written by Claude.

works.title: Last Skip
works.blurb: Your phone is the stone: throw it across a simulated pond and count the skips. Farewell mode counts the real bounces and sends them live to a friend, down to the last splash.

works.title: Ashland
works.blurb: A quiet game set in Ashland State Park, Massachusetts, rebuilt from real map and elevation data and played through the four seasons. Row the lake, fish it, cut a tree if you must. Everything you ask a machine to do costs the place something, and it doesn't grow back overnight.

works.title: Orbitakt
works.blurb: A drum machine played by the satellites overhead. A radar beam sweeps round your sky, and every satellite it passes hits a drum, with a dub echo that opens whenever one crosses the zenith. Live orbits, worked out in your browser.

works.title: Musicbox
works.blurb: A music box in a Swiss cabin, built from its physics: wind it up, turn the crank by drawing circles on the screen, or let your pet hamster run the wheel. A comb of tuned tines does the playing, and the holiday tunes are in the box.

works.title: Cognitive Hands
works.blurb: Two virtual hands try to type a sentence, run by theories of how the mind orders its actions. Pick one of four models and watch it steer the same fingers, which have real joint limits, on a keyboard where a slip lands on the wrong key. It's a working prototype that asks whether these theories could run a body at all.

works.title: Comic Booklet
works.blurb: Five comics made by hand, bound into a little picture book you page through on the site. One is a single panel, one is twelve, one is a pair of frames you can cross your eyes to fuse, and one is a caption on a photo.

pages.alt: A cook in an apron eats a roasted leg while an angel lies on the counter: "Yum! Tastes like chicken!"
A twelve-panel strip: a desert road, a boulder, and a very unlucky coyote, ending on a close-up of a worried face.
A Dutch cartoon: a patient on a therapist's couch says nobody takes him seriously; the doctor asks who made a mess on his sofa.
Two side-by-side frames, each with a tiny figure alone on an empty page, meant to be fused by crossing your eyes.
A black-and-white concert photo of a performer in sunglasses and a military-style jacket, with a joke caption in script lettering at the lower right.
